clue.text: Crowd round line on frozen water — absurd!

indicators.note: the crowd's letters go round the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: to crowd is to press

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece 'on' another follows it

parts.note: frozen water is ice

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a crowd gathered round a line drawn on an icy pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Priceless is informal for hilariously ridiculous, so an absurd situation can be called priceless.

clue.text: Boozy night out, rising up fighting, carrying clubs

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word up is read from bottom to top
the fighting word holds the clubs letter within it

parts.note: a brawl is a fight
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A rowdy evening out ends with a fight breaking out and weapons being carried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' looks like weapons in a brawl, but it is the card suit, giving C.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is a drinking tour moving from one bar to the next over an evening.

clue.text: Tattoo covered by wrinkles

indicators.note: the answer sits concealed within the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A tattoo becomes hidden among the creases of ageing skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink someone is slang for giving them a tattoo, so the verbs match.

clue.text: First to escape, stick in a northerly direction and run away

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the letters are read upwards, back to front
takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a pole is a stick

explanation.surface: An escapee grabs a pole, heads north and makes a getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of E plus POLE, EPOLE, is turned around, not just the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, usually to marry.

clue.text: Face fever scene, suppressing a twisted liveliness

indicators.note: the remaining letters are wrenched into a new order
the letter a is held down and removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone confronts a feverish scene, holding back a contorted expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A from FACE FEVER SCENE ('suppressing a') and rearrange the thirteen letters left ('twisted').
explanation.definitionFit: Effervescence, literally fizzing bubbles, is used figuratively for bubbly high spirits.

clue.text: Guide for artists confused clients

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: An art supplier's customers are baffled by a guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out template that painters follow to reproduce a shape.

clue.text: Rob someone who is easily fooled

definitions.meaning: to rob someone in the street

explanation.definitionFit: Mug is both a verb for street robbery and British slang for a gullible victim.

clue.text: Ship's month on river?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: May is a month
a crossword river is something that flows, a flower; the question mark flags the pun

explanation.surface: A question about which month a ship sailed upriver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' is a 'flow-er', not a named river. The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower is the famous vessel that carried English settlers across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Opening grid without resistance

indicators.note: the resistance letter is left out of the grid word

parts.note: a grate is a metal grid
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A gap in a grille offers no resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is an opening in a wall or fence through which one passes.

clue.text: Cooking competition cancelled after beginnings of brawl about kitchen equipment

indicators.note: the cancelled word comes after the initials
take the first letter of each of the next four words

parts.note: an event called off is off

explanation.surface: A cooking contest is called off after a fight over kitchen gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about kitchen equipment' reads as the subject of the brawl, but those words only give initials. The Great British Bake Off is a hugely popular TV baking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bake-off is a baking contest, as in the British television show.

clue.text: State regularly set Guy's path

indicators.note: take every second letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone has laid out a route for Guy.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a sovereign country, and state here means nation.

clue.text: Row of peeled fruit

indicators.note: the fruit loses its outer letter, as if its skin were stripped

parts.note: an orange is a fruit

explanation.surface: A line of skinned fruit laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: A range, as of mountains, is a row or line of things.

clue.text: Broadcast of e-lesson is inaudible

indicators.note: scattering seed widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An online lesson's transmission has no sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noiseless makes no sound, so it cannot be heard.

clue.text: Order return of Conservative taken in by true Liberal

indicators.note: the Conservative letter is placed inside the rest

parts.note: real means true

explanation.surface: Political talk of a Tory welcomed back by a genuine Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something, like a faulty product or an ambassador, is to demand that it come back.

clue.text: Extend makeshift cart or pimp up somewhat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters are read bottom to top
only part of the phrase supplies the letters, concealed within it

explanation.surface: Someone stretches a homemade cart, or tarts it up a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' hides TCARTORP across 'makeshift cart or pimp', and 'up' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or draw something out in time.

clue.text: Well, sir, we both ruffled informant

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters are mussed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims to a gentleman that the two of them are flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistleblower informs on wrongdoing within an organisation.

clue.text: Spooner's trendy bird's bag of tricks

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: cool means trendy
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A fashionable bird owns a set of tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of COOL TIT gives TOOL KIT; the C of COOL is spoken as K.
explanation.definitionFit: A toolkit is figuratively the set of skills or resources someone can draw on, a bag of tricks.

clue.text: Epic finale of piece choir butchered

indicators.note: mangled, so these letters are hacked into a new order
take the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A choir murders the last movement of a grand piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means grand and heroic in scale, like the deeds of a legendary hero.

clue.text: Nevertheless protecting sailors damaged by fire

indicators.note: the outer word shields the sailors by surrounding them

parts.note: but means nevertheless
RN is the Royal Navy, crossword sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors are protected regardless, yet something was scorched.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt describes anything scorched or harmed by flames.

clue.text: Book by Roman poet relating to cattle?

parts.note: Ovid was a Roman poet, author of the Metamorphoses

explanation.surface: A book by a classical poet about cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bovid relates to the family Bovidae, which includes cattle; the question mark flags that it is wider.

clue.text: Do as instructed, honour head of year

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

indicators.note: take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A pupil follows orders and respects the head of their school year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of year' is a British school teacher in charge of a year group; here 'head of' only gives a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey is to comply with commands given.

clue.text: On the phone, slow down and disconnect

indicators.note: heard over a phone line, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: to brake is to slow down

explanation.surface: A caller is told to slow down and then hangs up.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a circuit or connection is to sever it.

clue.text: Short story of knight with naked lover repelled everyone

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: the word is stripped of its outer letters, leaving its middle
driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A tale of a knight whose unclothed lover put everyone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, longer than a short story but much shorter than a full-length book.

clue.text: Ultimately, apocryphal yeti tale is falsehood

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A dubious tale about a yeti turns out to be untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is a deliberate untruth.

clue.text: Agreed, in the past you succeeded

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Confirmation that someone did well in earlier days.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes as an exclamation expresses agreement.

clue.text: Passes through river hotter than any other

indicators.note: the passes word runs through the middle of the river

parts.note: the Trent is an English river
to pass away is to die, so passes means dies

explanation.surface: Something crosses a river and is hotter than anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands. 'Passes through' looks like crossing; 'Passes' means DIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot means fashionable, so the hottest thing is the most trendy.
